1.0 INTRODUCTION:

1.1 To establish guidelines and policy for prescription of medications for all health care practitioners involved in this process.

2.0 SCOPE:

2.1 This policy is applicable Hospital side to all clinical areas

3.0 RESPONSIBILTY:

3.1 All doctors

3.2 Pharmacist

4.0 ABBREVIATION:

4.1 NABH : National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare providers

4.2 MOM : Management of Medication

5.0 DEFINITION: Nil

6.0 REFERENCE:

6.1 NABH: Accreditation Standards For Ayurveda Hospitals 2nd Edition April 2016.

7.0 OBJECTIVE ELEMENTS

7.1 Documented policies and procedures exist for prescription of medication.

7.2 The organizations determine the minimum requirements of a prescription.

7.3 The organization determines who can write orders.

7.4 Orders are written in a uniform location in the medical records.

7.5 Medication orders are clear, legible, dated, timed, named and signed.

7.6 Medication orders contain the name of the medicine, route of administration, dose to be administered and frequency/time of administration.

7.7 Policy on verbal orders is documented and implemented.

7.8 The organization defines a list of high alert medications.

7.9 High alert medication orders are verified prior to dispensing.

8.0 PROCEDURES:

8.1 Hospital has documented policies and procedures for prescription of medications

8.2 All medical practitioners use only standard Prescription format of hospital for prescribing medications for the patients and every prescription contains the date, name of the patient, unique hospital number, name of the drug, dose, route and frequency of administration of the medicine, name, and signature of the prescribing doctor. Whenever there is doubt regarding a particular prescription (such as illegible handwriting, wrongly written strength/dose or frequency, doubt regarding similar sounding medicines, duplication etc.,) or when a prescription is incomplete (without sign, date, etc.), the junior doctor/pharmacist /nurse are promptly call the Doctor and get it corrected without causing inconvenience for patient

8.3 In hospital only registered/credentialed doctors can write orders, telephonic orders are countersigned within 24 hrs.

8.4 All orders are written on right side of case paper

8.5 Medication orders are clear, legible, in block letter, dated, timed, named and signed. Only approved abbreviations are used by the organization.

8.6 Organization assures medication orders contain the name of the medicine, route of administration, dose to be administered and frequency/time of administration.

8.7 Hospital ensures that the procedure incorporate good practices like “read back”. Verbal orders (if any) to on duty sister shall be counter-signed by the doctor who ordered it within 24 hours of ordering.

8.8 Annexure

8.9 Hospital ensures high alert medications order are verified prior to dispensing
